cls: Recombinant viral protein subunit vaccine (VLP / non-infectious)
pharm: Active immunizing agent / oncogenic virus prevention
quick: Age 9-14: 2 doses (0, 6 months); Age >=15 (or immunocompromised): 3 doses (0, 1-2, 6 months) IM 0.5 mL
Intramuscular into deltoid muscle; shake vigorously before injection
Not recommended during pregnancy; if initiated before pregnancy, delay remaining doses until postpartum
>95-99% prevention of high-grade cervical dysplasia (CIN2/3) and anogenital warts from targeted types
Syncope / vasovagal reaction: observe patient seated for 15 minutes post-injection
summary: Human papillomavirus (HPV) recombinant vaccines (bivalent [types 16, 18], quadrivalent [6, 11, 16, 18], or 9-valent [6, 11, 16, 18, 31, 33, 45, 52, 58]) contain non-infectious virus-like particles (VLPs) of the major capsid (L1) protein produced by recombinant DNA technology. They prevent persistent HPV infection and precancerous lesions (dysplasia) of the cervix, vulva, vagina, penis, anus, and oropharynx, as well as anogenital warts. Standard routine target age is 9 to 14 years before sexual debut, but vaccination is approved and beneficial up to age 26 (and shared clinical decision-making up to age 45).
indications: Prevention of cervical, vulvar, vaginal, penile, anal, and oropharyngeal precancerous lesions and cancers caused by high-risk oncogenic HPV types
Prevention of condyloma acuminata (anogenital warts) caused by HPV types 6 and 11 (quadrivalent and 9-valent vaccines)
Recommended routinely for all adolescents (girls and boys) starting at age 9 to 14 years
Catch-up vaccination for females and males through age 26; clinical consideration in adults aged 27 to 45 years

dosage.d: 0.5 mL IM at Month 0 and Month 6-12
dosage.n: If second dose is administered earlier than 5 months after the first dose, a third dose must be given at least 4 months after the second.

dosage.d: 0.5 mL IM at Month 0, Month 1-2, and Month 6
dosage.n: All immunocompromised persons (including HIV infection, solid organ transplant) require the full 3-dose series regardless of age at initiation.

dosage.d: 0.5 mL IM at Month 0, Month 2, and Month 6
dosage.n: Based on shared clinical decision-making; most beneficial in persons with few prior sexual partners.

admin: Administer strictly intramuscularly in the deltoid region of the upper arm.
Shake the vial or prefilled syringe vigorously before administration to maintain a cloudy, uniform suspension.
Post-vaccination syncope (vasovagal fainting) is common in adolescents: keep the patient seated or lying down during administration and observe for 15 minutes post-injection.
Do not freeze; store between 2°C and 8°C protected from light.
moa: Purified recombinant L1 capsid protein self-assembles into hollow, non-infectious virus-like particles (VLPs). Upon intramuscular injection, VLPs induce high titers of type-specific neutralizing serum IgG antibodies (transudating onto mucosal surfaces) that bind to incoming HPV virions and prevent viral entry into basal epithelial cells during micro-trauma, blocking persistent infection and subsequent oncogenic neoplastic transformation.

absolute: Severe acute anaphylactic hypersensitivity to yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) for quadrivalent/9-valent vaccines or to a prior dose of HPV vaccine
relative: Pregnancy: defer remaining doses until postpartum (pregnancy test is not required before vaccination, but do not deliberately vaccinate while pregnant)
Moderate to severe acute febrile illness (defer vaccination until recovered)
monitor: Syncope (fainting), transient lightheadedness, dizziness (especially in adolescents)

preg: Not recommended during pregnancy. If a woman is found to be pregnant after initiating the series, remaining doses should be delayed until completion of pregnancy. No evidence of teratogenicity if inadvertently given.
lact: Safe. Compatible with breastfeeding; lactating women may receive HPV vaccine without disruption.
serious_se: Vasovagal syncope with fall / head injury (preventable by seated observation)
monitoring: Keep patient seated or recumbent for 15 minutes post-vaccination to prevent syncope-related falls

Cervical cancer screening (Pap smear / HPV DNA) MUST continue per routine guidelines regardless of vaccination status (vaccines do not protect against all oncogenic HPV types or pre-existing infections)
